new_symbol_range_suggestions.P_CO2: positive, experimentally varied across physiologic-to-elevated equilibrating carbon dioxide tensions
new_symbol_range_suggestions.co2_affinity_shift: nonnegative, small enough that 1 + co2_affinity_shift*P_CO2 stays positive over the sampled P_CO2 range
new_symbol_range_suggestions.variant_co2_affinity_shift: nonnegative, small enough that 1 + variant_co2_affinity_shift*P_CO2 stays positive over the sampled P_CO2 range

derivation_notes: The added mechanism releases carbon dioxide tension as an explicit sampled environment and lets it increase the effective affinity scale denominator for each hemoglobin subpopulation, implementing a Bohr/carbamino-like right shift of the oxygen dissociation curve. Differential baseline-versus-variant carbon dioxide sensitivity creates a joint dependence on P_CO2 and hemoglobin composition while preserving bounded low- and high-pressure limits.
change_summary: The successor adds carbon-dioxide-dependent modulation of effective P50 for both baseline and variant hemoglobin branches. This creates an observable P_O2-by-P_CO2 interaction in equilibrium saturation that the parent cannot express when one shared parameter set must cover samples collected at multiple carbon dioxide tensions.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: Carbon dioxide tension directly shifts effective oxygen affinity at equilibrium through Bohr/carbamino regulation, and the shift can differ between baseline and variant hemoglobin subpopulations.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: Set co2_affinity_shift = 0 and variant_co2_affinity_shift = 0, or hold P_CO2 fixed so its effect is absorbed into constant effective affinity scales.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: Across samples with the same P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, higher P_CO2 lowers S_O2 mainly in the mid-saturation region, with weak separation near zero loading and reduced separation near the plateau; if variant_co2_affinity_shift differs from co2_affinity_shift, the size of that shift also changes with hemoglobin_variant_fraction.

response_change.parent_relation: S_O2 depends only on P_O2 and a sample-level variant mixture, so all curvature changes are attributed to hemoglobin subpopulation weighting and fixed cooperative parameters under one held environment.
response_change.child_relation: S_O2 depends on P_O2 and an added independently varied carbon dioxide tension that shifts effective affinity and can differentially modulate baseline and variant occupancy curves, creating a P_O2-by-environment interaction in the equilibrium saturation mapping.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, samples exposed to higher carbon dioxide tension show lower saturation mainly over the mid-loading range, with little separation near zero pressure and a compressed difference near the plateau.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when equilibrated samples are compared across independently imposed carbon dioxide tensions large enough to shift effective affinity, especially for intermediate reduced pressures near the transition region; the effect is weak at very low P_O2 and vanishes as saturation approaches the bounded plateau.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as systematic mid-range horizontal/shape shifts across imposed environment values at fixed P_O2 and composition; in holdout, the same interaction extends to unseen combinations of P_O2 and variant fraction without changing the low- and high-pressure limits.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when carbon dioxide tension is fixed across all samples or when the new environment-coupling coefficient tends to zero, so effective affinity and cooperative shape no longer vary with that added condition.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: The current contract holds acid-base and carbon dioxide conditions fixed, so no existing symbol can represent the known Bohr/carbamino environmental modulation. A new independently sampled static input is required to make that interaction observable in the scored equilibrium mapping rather than hidden inside refit constants.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Bohr/carbamino regulation alters hemoglobin allosteric balance and effective oxygen affinity at equilibrium, shifting oxygen loading differently across the pressure range and potentially differently for baseline versus variant hemoglobin fractions.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than retuning a coefficient because the effective reduced-pressure coordinates now depend jointly on P_O2 and the new environment input P_CO2, and differential baseline/variant sensitivity introduces composition-dependent environmental interaction rather than one globally fixed curve family.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Carbon dioxide tension is constant and therefore has no explicit role in the saturation curve.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Carbon dioxide tension is an independently varied equilibrium environment that shifts effective affinity, with potentially different sensitivity in baseline and variant hemoglobin branches.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, increasing P_CO2 lowers saturation predominantly through the transition region while leaving the near-zero and near-plateau limits almost unchanged; if variant_co2_affinity_shift differs from co2_affinity_shift, the P_CO2 effect changes systematically with mixture fraction.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this signature across multiple imposed P_CO2 values because the parent has no carbon-dioxide input at all, so it predicts identical S_O2 for samples sharing P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction regardless of environment. Refitting all existing parent parameters can fit at most one common compromise curve family over the pooled conditions, but cannot generate an explicit within-model P_O2-by-P_CO2 interaction with preserved low- and high-saturation limits across those same conditions.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as systematic mid-range horizontal/shape shifts across imposed environment values at fixed P_O2 and composition; in holdout, the same interaction extends to unseen combinations of P_O2 and variant fraction without changing the low- and high-pressure limits.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: The current contract holds acid-base and carbon dioxide conditions fixed, so no existing symbol can represent the known Bohr/carbamino environmental modulation. A new independently sampled static input is required to make that interaction observable in the scored equilibrium mapping rather than hidden inside refit constants.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model omits sample-to-sample environmental modulation of equilibrium oxygen affinity by carbon dioxide tension, forcing all observed dissociation-curve variation to be explained only by P50_O2 and hemoglobin subpopulation composition.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Carbon dioxide tension is constant and therefore has no explicit role in the saturation curve.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Bohr/carbamino regulation alters hemoglobin allosteric balance and effective oxygen affinity at equilibrium, shifting oxygen loading differently across the pressure range and potentially differently for baseline versus variant hemoglobin fractions.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already maps equilibrium saturation as a weighted sum of baseline and variant Adair-like binding curves, with P_O2 varied and temperature, acidity, and carbon dioxide held fixed. A realistic next refinement is to release carbon dioxide tension as an independently varied condition because hemoglobin oxygen loading is well known to depend on it even at equilibrium. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary interpretation: for the same P_O2 and hemoglobin_variant_fraction, the child predicts different S_O2 across carbon dioxide conditions. The concrete contrast is that higher carbon dioxide lowers effective affinity, so the saturation difference is largest around the transition region and small near both the zero-loading and high-pressure plateau limits. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce that pattern across multiple imposed carbon dioxide tensions because the parent has no environmental input; it can only fit one common curve family over all such samples, or absorb one condition at the expense of another. The effect is scientifically admissible when carbon dioxide tension is intentionally varied while other within-sample conditions remain controlled or co-adjusted so monotone bounded saturation is preserved. If carbon dioxide is truly fixed experimentally, this mechanism cannot activate and the parent remains adequate.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make one process depend jointly on two declared quantities.

scenario_text: Measure the fractional oxygen saturation of hemoglobin in equilibrated blood samples across independently imposed oxygen partial pressures. The response reflects cooperative oxygen loading within erythrocytes and should transition from weak loading at low pressure to a high-pressure plateau. Temperature, acidity, carbon dioxide tension, and hemoglobin composition are held fixed so that oxygen partial pressure is the only sampled condition. The benchmark targets the instantaneous equilibrium saturation rather than the kinetics of gas exchange.
promotion_reason: The current contract holds acid-base and carbon dioxide conditions fixed, so no existing symbol can represent the known Bohr/carbamino environmental modulation. A new independently sampled static input is required to make that interaction observable in the scored equilibrium mapping rather than hidden inside refit constants.
